text:
alice: quick heads up — hit a repeatable OOM on a tp=8 run with batch=4 after kernel selection change. stacktrace points to temporary comm allocations during all-reduce. attaching compact profile snippet below.

alice: nvprof output (trimmed):
```
GPU 0: malloc 128MB at 0x7f...
GPU 1: NCCL temp alloc 192MB at 0x8a...
GPU 2: malloc 64MB at 0x9b...
Aggregate transient memory peak: ~3.2GB (worker workspace + NCCL staging)
```

ben: ugh. I think the kernel selector started preferring the tiled-conv path which raises workspace per-shard. combined with our per-request comm staging it oversubscribes. :thinking_face:

carla: do we have a repro script? can we toggle kernel selector back to old heuristic to confirm?

alice: repro branch: https://git.redwood/repro/tp-oom-snap. also added a minimal trace in /tmp/oom-trace.txt showing interleaved malloc/free and ncclCommAlloc calls.

infra-bot: scheduled a CI run on repro branch (gpu-large) — job id 9844. expected ~40m.

ben: short-term mitigation idea: introduce a comm_pool_reserve per node that preallocates a bounded slab for NCCL staging and mark it as non-evictable during collective. if pool fails, fall back to smaller all-reduce algorithm (reduce-scatter+allgather) which uses less staging.

carla: long-term I'd rather we change workspace sizing: make kernel selector ask allocator for "max_safe_workspace(gpu_id, headroom_pct)" instead of using static estimates. then selector can pick an algorithm whose worst-case plus comm-reserve stays below device capacity.

dmitri: also we should tweak batching heuristic: collapse micro-batches that share prefix KV cache into a single multi-beam step to reuse KV and reduce temporary transients. that lowers simultaneous workspace pressure across TP shards.

alice: yes — noted. My profiling shows the worst peaks happen when 3 shards concurrently allocate staging + kernel workspace + KV prefetch. if we stagger prefetch across micro-batches or reuse a shared prefetch buffer, peak drops by ~25% in our sim.

ben: prototype plan i can run this week: (1) add comm_pool_reserve knob + fallback path, (2) allocator query API for headroom-aware workspace, (3) small batching change to collapse tiny-prefix requests. will do isolated perf runs.

carla: ping me when you have a patch, I can wire the selector to the allocator API. add perf counters: comm_pool_used, workspace_requested, kv_prefetch_inflight. we need time-series to correlate spikes.

dmitri: test matrix: tp=[4,8,16], batch=[1,2,4], prefix_len=[0,8,64], kernel_mode=[old, new]. capture aggregate peak, tail latency, and failed_allocs.

alice: adding an entry to incidents channel with short blurb in case this reproduces in prod. for now, throttling the rollout of kernel selector change to 10% of capacity.

ben: small code hint for allocator API (pseudocode):
```
// ask allocator how much workspace we can safely request
size_t max_ws = allocator.max_safe_workspace(gpu_id, /*headroom_pct=*/12);
if (kernel_workspace <= max_ws) select_fast_kernel(); else select_memory_light_kernel();
```

carla: nice. also consider tagging some buffers as "comm_shared" so they can be re-used across shards when layout-compatible. reduces duplication.

alice: great ideas — let's track in the PR. infra-bot will post CI results. folks, please add any quick perf numbers to the thread. thanks! :raised_hands:
